newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi says jobs decree law must be quick.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi says jobs decree law must be quick.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Saturday that a planned government decree law aimed at creating new jobs must be a "streamlined measure" that can be approved quickly by parliament.

Ciampi said in a statement issued by the Treasury that the decree law would also oblige all administrations concerned to take "even more severe action in containing current spending so as not to prejudice the European objective".

Italian newspapers reported on Saturday that Ciampi was concerned that the decree law would bring a burden of additional expenditure which Italy, determined to be in the vanguard of a single European currency, could not afford.
The Corriere della Sera newspaper put the figure at around 11 trillion lire.

A cabinet meeting on Friday put back until next week approval of a package of measures agreed on Thursday at a meeting of the leaders of all main parties backing the centre-left government. "It will be approved at the next meeting," a cabinet statement said
Newspapers said the postponement followed objections raised by Ciampi to the increased spending.
The package includes provisions aimed at cutting the working week, introducing more flexible work contracts and boosting apprenticeship schemes.

Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni said the package had strengthened the 10-month old government while Fausto Bertinotti, leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation, said it would create 100,000 new jobs in the underdeveloped south.
Ciampi said the urgent problem that had to be confronted was unemployment in the more backward south.
"The initiatives to be speeded up are those that produce development. The decree law should smooth the procedures and should therefore be a streamlined measure," he said.
